'''Ōtomo no Takehi''' (大伴武日, also written as '''Ōtomo no Kenhi Muraji''' or '''Kenhi no Mikoto''') was a [[Kofun period]] figure mentioned in the [[Nihon Shoki]] and other historical records. He held the [[kabane]] (hereditary title) of [[Muraji]] and was the son of [[Toyohi no Mikoto]], an official in the [[Kōrei]] and {{ill|Kaika|en|Kaika|qid=Q14867060|lt=Kaika}} periods.

== Overview ==
In the [[Nihon Shoki]], he is referred to as "Ōtomo no Takehi Muraji" (大伴武日連) and is also mentioned in other texts as "Ōtomo no Kenhi Muraji" or "Kenhi no Mikoto." He does not appear in the [[Kojiki]]. He is considered a distant ancestor of the {{ill|Ōtomo clan|en|Ōtomo clan|qid=Q1096662|lt=Ōtomo Muraji}} (later Ōtomo clan). In the reign of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}, he was one of the five high officials and later became a retainer of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} during his eastern expedition under {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}.

== Records ==
According to the [[Nihon Shoki]], in the 25th year of {{ill|Emperor Suinin|en|Emperor Suinin|qid=Q314850|lt=Emperor Suinin}}'s reign (2nd month, 8th day), Takehi was one of the "great officials" (大夫, maetsukimi), alongside [[Takenukawawake]] (ancestor of the [[Abe clan|Abe no Omi]]), [[Hiko Kunifuki]] (ancestor of the {{ill|Wani clan|en|Wani clan|qid=Q11417873|lt=Wani no Omi}}), [[Kuni no Shima]] (ancestor of the [[Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi no Muraji]]), and [[Mononobe no Tokoneme]] (ancestor of the [[Mononobe clan|Mononobe no Muraji]]), and was entrusted with the duties of Shinto rituals.{{Sfn|Ōtomo no Takehi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}

[[File:Sakaorimiya shaden.jpg|thumb|200px|right|[[Sakaori Shrine]] ({{ill|Kōfu|en|Kōfu|qid=Q201932|lt=Kōfu}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|qid=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture}})<br />{{smaller|Traditionally identified as the "Sakaori Shrine" mentioned in the Nihon Shoki.}}]]
The [[Nihon Shoki]] also describes his role during the eastern expedition of {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} in the 40th year of {{ill|Emperor Keikō|en|Emperor Keikō|qid=Q329723|lt=Emperor Keikō}}'s reign. Along with [[Kibi no Takehiko]], he served as a retainer and received a ceremonial quiver from Yamato Takeru at [[Sakaori Shrine]] (traditionally identified with a site in present-day {{ill|Kōfu|en|Kōfu|qid=Q201932|lt=Kōfu}}, {{ill|Yamanashi Prefecture|en|Yamanashi Prefecture|qid=Q132720|lt=Yamanashi Prefecture}}).{{Sfn|Ōtomo no Takehi (Ancient Clans)|2010}}

In the [[Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]] entry for the 3rd year of {{ill|Jōgan|en|Jōgan|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} (861), the retainer [[Bando Yoshio]] recounts that Ōtomo no Kenhi Muraji assisted Yamato Takeru in pacifying the eastern provinces and was granted {{ill|Sanuki Province|en|Sanuki Province|qid=Q929682|lt=Sanuki Province}} as a reward. This account also mentions his descendants, including [[Ōtomo no Takei|Kenmochi (Takei/Kentake)]], and states that one of his line became a [[Sanuki no Kuni no Miyatsuko|provincial governor]] under {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|en|Emperor Ingyō|qid=Q349258|lt=Emperor Ingyō}}.{{Sfn|Ōtomo no Takehi (Historical Sources)}}

== Legends ==
In [[:en:Rikuzentakata|Rikuzentakata]], {{ill|Iwate Prefecture|en|Iwate Prefecture|qid=Q48326|lt=Iwate Prefecture}}, there is a local legend called the "Takehi Chōja Legend." According to this story, Takehi accompanied {{ill|Yamato Takeru|en|Yamato Takeru|qid=Q461258|lt=Yamato Takeru}} to [[Kesen District]] during the eastern expedition and fathered two daughters, Morning Sun Princess and Evening Sun Princess. A location in Ōishi, Takada Town, is said to be the site of Takehi Chōja's residence.
